## Italian Salary Components
URL: https://italybluecard.com/italy-salary-components.html
Summary: From the RAL in the offer to net pay: 13th and 14th month, employee contributions, IRPEF, surcharges, meal vouchers and benefits, explained for professionals moving to Italy.
 Employment guide Reading an Italian offer Italian offers quote the RAL, the annual gross salary. It is also the figure checked against the Blue Card threshold. What reaches your account each month depends on installments, contributions and tax.
Installments The RAL is split into 13 installments, or 14 under agreements such as Commerce and services: the 13th in December, the 14th in June or July. Both accrue month by month, so joining mid-year gives you the accrued part.
What is withheld Employee social security of 9.19% of gross pay, plus 1% on the part above €56,224 a year. IRPEF income tax: 23% up to €28,000, 33% from €28,000 to €50,000, 43% above, reduced by employment tax credits. Regional and municipal surcharges, depending on where you live. Pension contributions stop above a yearly ceiling of €122,295 in 2026 for people first insured from 1996, which includes anyone starting their Italian career now.
Try the net pay calculator.
Benefits worth knowing Meal vouchers: exempt up to €10 a day if electronic, €4 if paper (2026). Fringe benefits: tax-free up to €1,000 a year, €2,000 with dependent children (2026), useful once the family has joined. Housing: rent paid or reimbursed by the employer, common in relocation packages. Supplementary health: contributions to health funds exempt up to €3,615.20 a year. Productivity bonus: up to €5,000 a year taxed at a flat 1% in 2026, under a company agreement. On the employer's side The employer adds its own INPS share (around 30%), INAIL and the 6.91% TFR accrual. None of this reduces your pay; it is the cost the calculator shows.
More in the guide EOR, entity or contractors? The payroll calendar From RAL to net pay Contracts, leave and termination Running payroll from abroad Get a quote

## Italy Payroll Calendar

 Employment guide A year of Italian payroll Once the permit is granted and the person starts, payroll runs on a fixed monthly rhythm with a few yearly deadlines. Here is the calendar your finance team will see.
CurrencyEuro; your invoice in EUR or USD Tax year1 January - 31 December Pay frequencyMonthly, plus 13th (and sometimes 14th) month, which we spread pro rata on your invoices Taxes and contributionsPaid by the 16th of the following month (F24) Time zoneCET (UTC+1), CEST in summer Each month Mid-monthCut-off for overtime, absences, bonuses, joiners and leavers. Third weekCalculation and checks. End of monthNet pay transferred and payslips sent. 16th of next monthTaxes and INPS/INAIL contributions paid with the F24; UniEmens filed. The hire itself is reported electronically to the labour authorities the day before work starts. For a visa holder, that date follows the stay contract.

## Italy Quota Work Permits (Decreto Flussi)
URL: https://italybluecard.com/italy-work-permit-quotas.html
Summary: How the Decreto Flussi quota system works for non-EU workers in 2026: 43,300 non-seasonal entries, how they split, and when the Blue Card is the better route.
 Visa routes The quota route: Decreto Flussi If a role does not meet Blue Card conditions, the usual way in is an ordinary work permit within the annual entry quotas. Places are limited and applications open in set windows, so the calendar drives the plan.
2026 non-seasonal quotas GroupEntries 2026 Nationals of countries under art. 6, par. 2, letter a of the decree25,000 Nationals of countries with cooperation agreements with Italy18,000 Stateless persons and refugees300 Total non-seasonal43,300 What it means in practice Nationality decides the pool. Check the candidate's citizenship against the groups before any offer. Be ready before the window. Places are shared by all employers in Italy. Contract, housing and documents should be prepared before applications open. Prefer the Blue Card when you can. ## Italy vs Other EU Blue Card Countries
URL: https://italybluecard.com/italy-vs-eu-blue-card-countries.html
Summary: Italy compared with Germany and the Netherlands for Blue Card holders: salary thresholds, permanent residence, notice, leave, sick pay, contributions, 13th month, TFR and non-compete.
 EU Blue Card Italy, Germany or the Netherlands? The Blue Card is an EU scheme, but each country sets its own threshold and its own employment rules. Italy's threshold is much lower, which opens the route to more roles and earlier-career profiles. Here is how the three compare.
The employment contract Sources, read 4 Nov 2026. Italy: D.Lgs. 286/1998 art. 27-quater (text); threshold from arlettipartners.com; TFR Civil Code art. 2120. Germany: thresholds from The Local citing the Federal Foreign Office; settlement permit from service.berlin.de; notice from allaboutberlin.com citing BGB § 622. Netherlands: thresholds from IND; leave, holiday allowance and sick pay from L&E Global. General orientation, not legal advice.
What this means for a candidate A role paid above the Italian threshold but below €45,934.20 a year can qualify for a Blue Card in Italy while falling short of both German thresholds, and of the Dutch one. Living costs outside the biggest cities are lower too. In exchange, Italian employment is more structured: a CCNL sets the minimums, and pay is spread over 13 or 14 installments with TFR on top.
What this means for an employer abroad Budget the full Italian employment cost, not just the salary: contributions, 13th month and TFR. The calculator shows it month by month. Health care is public and not on your invoice.
Check a role against the thresholdBlue Card in Italy

## Net Pay in Italy Calculator
URL: https://italybluecard.com/net-pay-calculator.html
Summary: From gross to net in Italy in 2026: employee social security, income tax (IRPEF) with employment credits, regional and municipal surcharges, for Milan, Rome, Turin, Bologna and Naples.
 Net pay calculator What you will take home in Italy Moving to Italy on an offer quoted as annual gross (RAL)? Enter it with the city you plan to live in. The estimate applies 2026 rules: employee social security, income tax with employment credits and local surcharges.
Annual gross salary, RAL (EUR) CityMilanRomeTurinBolognaNaples Paid in13 installments14 installments12 (13th/14th pro-rata) ItemPer year How the calculation works The employee pays 9.19% social security on gross pay, plus 1% on the part above €56,224 a year. Income tax (IRPEF) applies to what remains: 23% up to €28,000, 33% from €28,000 to €50,000, 43% above. Employment tax credits reduce the tax. They are largest on low salaries and reach zero at €50,000. Between €20,000 and €40,000 an extra credit of up to €1,000 applies. The regional and municipal surcharges are added, unless income is below the city's exemption threshold. For the cost to the company employing you, see the employer cost calculator. For the Blue Card, the threshold is checked on gross salary, not on net pay.

URL: https://italybluecard.com/relocation-italy.html
Summary: Your first weeks in Italy after the visa: stay contract, residence permit, tax code, residence registration, health service, housing and bank account.
 Relocation From landing to first payslip The visa gets you through the border. A handful of appointments in the first weeks turn it into a life in Italy. We handle the employer side of each one and tell you exactly what to bring.
Stay contractYou and your employer (us) sign the contratto di soggiorno at the Sportello Unico per l'Immigrazione. Residence permitApplication through the postal kit, then fingerprints at the Questura. Keep the post office receipt: it shows the application is under way. Tax codeThe codice fiscale is needed for the contract, payroll, a lease and a bank account. Residence registrationRegistration at the municipal registry (anagrafe) at your address. Health serviceEnrolment with the national health service and choice of a family doctor. Bank accountAn Italian or EU account for your salary. HousingRental contracts are usually long term. A temporary furnished flat for the first weeks gives time to choose a neighbourhood, and the final lease supports any family reunification request.
DocumentsDegree, marriage and birth certificates issued outside the EU need legalisation or apostille and a certified translation. A CIMEA comparability statement can replace the declaration of value for degrees.
LanguageOffices work in Italian. We speak Italian and English and can come with you to the employer appointments.
Relocation service Beyond the permit, we can organise the tax code, the housing search, health service registration and the bank account. Quoted per case.
